name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
description: The straight-arm pulldown is a cable isolation exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi without recruiting the biceps, as the elbows remain locked throughout the movement. This makes it an effective tool for developing the mind-muscle connection to the lats and for pre-exhausting or finishing the back without fatiguing the elbow flexors.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a high-pulley cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart. Grasp a straight bar with both hands shoulder-width apart using a pronated grip. Take a step back and lean forward slightly from the hips, extending the arms overhead so the lats are on stretch.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a straight bar to the high pulley. Set the weight appropriately — this is an isolation exercise and heavier loads commonly break form. Position yourself far enough from the stack to feel lat tension at the start.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms fully extended overhead, feeling a stretch in the lats and a slight forward lean at the hips.
Step 2: Lock the elbows — they must not bend at any point during the movement.
Step 3: Drive the bar down toward your thighs in a wide arc by contracting the lats and depressing the shoulder blades.
Step 4: Lower the bar to touch the front of the thighs, maximally contracting the lats.
Step 5: Reverse the motion under control, allowing the arms to rise back to the starting position with the lats fully lengthened.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pull the bar down. Inhale as you return to the overhead starting position.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows — this recruits the biceps and reduces lat isolation
Using trunk flexion rather than lat contraction to drive the bar down
Insufficient range of motion by not allowing the arms to fully extend overhead
safety_considerations: Avoid rounding the lower back — maintain a neutral spine throughout
Do not load this exercise heavily; it is intended for isolation work
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension overhead at the start to the thighs at the bottom. The arc of movement should be smooth and consistent.
coaching_cues: Pretend your elbows are in a cast — they cannot bend
Lead the movement with the shoulder blades, not the hands
Think of crushing something between your lat and your hip
